record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: Let X2 be the free part of the full shift {0,1}^{Z^2} with shift action σ, let XH be the space of directed bi-infinite Hamiltonian paths in Z^2, and let Φ : (X2, σ) → (XH, σ) be a Borel equivariant map as in Theorem 3.2, inducing a Z-action T_Φ on X2. Can Φ be chosen so that for all invariant ergodic probability measures μ and ν on X2, the systems (X2, μ, σ) and (X2, ν, σ) are conjugate if and only if (X2, μ, T_Φ) and (X2, ν, T_Φ) are conjugate?

evidence.quote: Theorem 3.2. [20] There is a Borel equivariant map Φ from (X2, σ) to (XH, σ). One of the consequences of this result is that it gives a (very special) orbit equivalence from (X2, σ) to a Z Polish dynamical system which we denote henceforth by (X2, TΦ). In addition one has that if µ is an invariant ergodic probability measure for (X2, σ) then it is also an invariant ergodic probability measure for (X2, TΦ). Let Me denote the space of invariant probability measures for (X2, σ).
Question 3.3 (Chandgotia). Can Φ be chosen such that for all µ, ν ∈ Me, (X2, µ, σ) is conjugate to (X2, ν, σ) if and only if (X2, µ, TΦ) is conjugate to (X2, ν, TΦ)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X = \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}^2}$ with the natural shift action of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, and let $X_2 \subseteq X$ denote the free part of this action (i.e. the Borel set of points with trivial stabilizer). Write $\sigma$ for the restricted $\mathbb{Z}^2$-action on $X_2$. Let $X_H \subseteq (\mathbb{Z}^2)^{\mathbb{Z}}$ denote the Polish space of directed bi-infinite Hamiltonian paths in $\mathbb{Z}^2$, i.e. bijections $p:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}^2$ such that $p(n+1)-p(n)$ is a unit vector for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}$; equip $X_H$ with the natural $\mathbb{Z}^2$-action by translation (shifting the image by a vector in $\mathbb{Z}^2$), also denoted $\sigma$.

Assume there exists a Borel $\mathbb{Z}^2$-equivariant map $\Phi : (X_2,\sigma) \to (X_H,\sigma)$. Such a map induces a Borel $\mathbb{Z}$-action $T_\Phi$ on $X_2$ defined by following the Hamiltonian path: for $x\in X_2$, $T_\Phi(x) = \sigma_{v(x)}(x)$, where $v(x) = \Phi(x)(1)-\Phi(x)(0) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$. Every $\sigma$-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $X_2$ is then $T_\Phi$-invariant, and ergodicity is preserved. Let $M_e$ denote the set of ergodic $\sigma$-invariant Borel probability measures on $X_2$.

Question: Can $\Phi$ be chosen so that for all $\mu,\nu \in M_e$, the measure-preserving $\mathbb{Z}^2$-systems $(X_2,\mu,\sigma)$ and $(X_2,\nu,\sigma)$ are measurably conjugate if and only if the measure-preserving $\mathbb{Z}$-systems $(X_2,\mu,T_\Phi)$ and $(X_2,\nu,T_\Phi)$ are measurably conjugate?
artifact.status_search_result: The question, attributed to Chandgotia, appears in a recent compilation of open problems in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems. Web searches return related works of Chandgotia and Meyerovitch on Borel embeddings into subshifts and Hamiltonian path spaces, but no source claiming a resolution. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Borel factors and embeddings of systems in subshifts
status_evidence.snippet: The space of bi-infinite Hamiltonian paths is among several examples on Z^d shift spaces studied in this context.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study Hamiltonian path systems and Borel equivariant maps, with no resolution of the conjugacy question reported.

status_evidence.title: Borel subsystems and ergodic universality for compact Z^d-systems (Chandgotia–Meyerovitch)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes Borel equivariant maps from free Z^d shifts to Hamiltonian path systems and related universality.
status_evidence.claim: This is the source result (Theorem 3.2) providing the map Φ; subsequent literature does not report a positive or negative answer to the conjugacy question.
